method: For each PDF page 25-48, re-rendered the page in isolation (pdftoppm -r 220 -f N -l N) and visually re-read it fresh, independent of the original Scan B session's memory/description. Then grep'd a short, distinctive phrase from the fresh read against all 24 committed pages/pNN.json files to find where (if anywhere) that content actually landed, rather than trusting either session's recollection alone.

reliability_summary.root_cause_hypothesis: INFERENCE, not FACT: the six affected pages were all processed via 4-page parallel batch Read calls in the original Scan-B session (two batches: {28,29,30,31} and {32,33,34,35}, plus page 38 read as part of a {36,37,38,39} batch). Pages read individually/solo, or in smaller batches, were verified accurate in every case checked. This strongly suggests the error mechanism was cross-talk between images returned in the same multi-image tool response when the authoring agent wrote up several JSON files afterward from a blended/misordered memory of 4 images at once, rather than a fault in the underlying PDF rendering (the rendered PNG files themselves were independently confirmed correct via isolated single-page re-renders matching the original batch-rendered files byte-for-byte via md5).
